IR.rationale: A rising 5Y-FF spread signals tighter expected policy and higher discount rates, which tends to weigh on near-term equity returns.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark a credit shock. Such shocks raise required risk premia and often precede partial equity recovery.

V.rationale: High implied volatility embeds a large variance risk premium, and investors are compensated with higher subsequent equity returns.

AP.rationale: Strong recent market excess returns tend to partly reverse at weekly-to-monthly horizons through liquidity provision and overreaction.

ST.rationale: Conservative-investment firms outperforming signals a defensive rotation that has historically been followed by better market returns.

FX.rationale: A strong Australian dollar reflects risk-on carry positioning. That positioning is crowded and leaves equities exposed to reversal.

COM.rationale: Rising oil prices signal firm global demand, which supports cyclical earnings expectations.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions restrict funding and risk-taking, which predicts weaker equity returns.

ENDG.rationale: Unusually strong recent index returns tend to mean-revert at short horizons.

IR.rationale: A flattening curve signals tightening or deteriorating growth expectations, both associated with rising equity risk.

B.rationale: Credit stress transmits to equity through leverage and default risk, and it raises future realised variance.

V.rationale: Implied volatility contains forward-looking information about variance beyond what recent realised variance already captures.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage effect, falling prices raise volatility. A joint US and EM selloff indicates a global risk-off episode with persistent turbulence.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects a flight to quality that tends to accompany rising market volatility.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects safe-haven demand and carry unwinds, both of which precede higher equity volatility.

COM.rationale: Falling broad commodity prices signal weakening global demand and deflationary stress, which raise equity uncertainty.

MC.rationale: Tightening financial conditions combined with falling inflation expectations mark a deflationary stress state, which is linked to higher future variance.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is mean-reverting, so already elevated realised variance tends to be followed by less excess variance than its level implies.

IR.rationale: Bull steepening, with front-end yields falling on expected easing, tends to occur when growth fears intensify and downside risk rises.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads signal rising default risk and tighter funding, which raise crash risk in equities.

V.rationale: Broad cross-asset implied volatility signals a high-uncertainty regime with fat left tails.

AP.rationale: Small-cap underperformance reflects deteriorating liquidity and risk appetite, a precursor of broader drawdowns.

ST.rationale: Weak short-term reversal returns indicate impaired liquidity provision, which amplifies the risk of large price declines.

FX.rationale: Yen strength signals carry unwinds and safe-haven flows that coincide with equity crash risk.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices signal weakening demand and stress in energy credit, which raises left-tail risk.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions constrain intermediaries and are a well-documented predictor of downside tail risk.

ENDG.rationale: Recent own returns carry little consistent information about the probability of a large loss.

IR.rationale: Falling medium-term rate expectations signal anticipated easing, which can spark sharp equity rallies.

B.rationale: A credit stress state raises risk premia, and rebounds from it produce large equity gains.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and marks capitulation states from which strong rebounds are likely.

AP.rationale: After weak market returns, short-horizon reversal makes large rebounds more likely.

ST.rationale: Defensive rotation into conservative-investment stocks marks depressed sentiment, which precedes upside surprises.

FX.rationale: Safe-haven yen appreciation indicates risk-off positioning that sets up sharp relief rallies.

COM.rationale: Commodity weakness reflects risk-off states with elevated dispersion, from which outsized equity gains can follow.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress widens the return distribution and raises the chance of large policy- or relief-driven rallies.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent index returns raise the probability of a large rebound through short-horizon mean reversion.
